facts.text: Beau-Rivage Geneva is at 13 quai du Mont-Blanc in Geneva.
facts.excerpt: 13, quai du Mont-Blanc, 1201 Geneva, Switzerland

facts.text: Rooms are available from 3 p.m. on arrival day and must be vacated by noon on departure day.
facts.excerpt: Rooms are available from 3:00 p.m. on the day of arrival and must be vacated no later than 12:00 noon on the day of departure.

facts.text: All rooms, suites and indoor areas are strictly non-smoking.
facts.excerpt: All rooms, suites and indoor areas are strictly non-smoking.

facts.text: Pets are accepted with the hotel's prior approval, at an extra charge.
facts.excerpt: Pets are accepted subject to the Hotel's prior approval and incur additional charges.

facts.text: Baby cots are free with prior reservation.
facts.excerpt: Baby cots are available free of charge with prior reservation.

facts.text: The Geneva cantonal tourist tax is charged on top of the room rate.
facts.excerpt: The Geneva Cantonal tourist tax and any services not expressly included shall be charged in addition

facts.text: The Beau-Rivage opened in 1865.
facts.excerpt: The Beau-Rivage opened in 1865.

facts.text: The Mayer family owned the hotel for 155 years.
facts.excerpt: For 155 years it was owned by the Mayer family.

facts.text: At the end of 2020 the Mayers sold the hotel to another family, the Casacubertas.
facts.excerpt: Then, at the end of 2020, the Mayers sold the hotel to another family, the Casacubertas, from

facts.text: The hotel faces Lake Geneva from the Quai du Mont-Blanc, looking across to the Jet d'Eau.
facts.excerpt: opposite, the mesmeric plume of the Jet d'Eau, the stately façades of the Quai Gustave-Ador and the spire of St Peter's Cathedral.

facts.text: In the lobby, salmon-coloured columns rise from a mosaic-tiled floor.
facts.excerpt: Soaring, salmon-coloured columns rise from a mosaic-tiled floor

facts.text: Rooms mix Victorian, Edwardian, Art Nouveau and Art Deco design elements, and vary in mood from room to room.
facts.excerpt: depending on the size, situation and particular admixture of Victorian, Edwardian, Art Nouveau and Art Deco design elements.

facts.text: The facade is not straight along the Quai du Mont-Blanc but has several angles, which changes the lake outlook.
facts.excerpt: its façade is not straight and, as you might expect, parallel to the Quai du Mont-Blanc, but has several angles.

facts.text: Le Chat-Botte, the main fine-dining restaurant, opened in 1967.
facts.excerpt: The main fine-dining restaurant, Le Chat-Botté, opened in 1967 and remains a thriving local institution.

facts.text: The outdoor restaurant La Terrasse becomes La Terrasse Alpine in winter, with heated vintage gondola cabins from Gstaad.
facts.excerpt: La Terrasse—which becomes La Terrasse Alpine in the winter months, with heated vintage gondola cabins from Gstaad.

facts.text: Le Patara, downstairs, is a Thai restaurant.
facts.excerpt: Downstairs is a Thai restaurant, Le Patara.

facts.text: Albertine's, the little bar off the lobby, was formerly a reading room.
facts.excerpt: Formerly a reading room, it retains a certain serene seriousness of purpose

facts.text: The spa is a single treatment room, the Bellefontaine Suite, where one therapist looks after one guest at a time.
facts.excerpt: the Beau-Rivage makes do with a single treatment room—its Bellefontaine Suite—in which one therapist takes care of one guest at a time.

facts.text: In 1898 Empress Elisabeth of Austria, a guest at the hotel, was stabbed outside it and died in her suite shortly after.
facts.excerpt: She was a guest at the hotel at the time and died in her suite shortly after the attack.

facts.text: A cabinet holds a pair of Empress Elisabeth's gloves and a piece of bloodstained ribbon.
facts.excerpt: There is a cabinet containing a pair of her gloves and a piece of bloodstained ribbon.

facts.text: A small bronze plaque outside marks the spot where Empress Elisabeth was attacked.
facts.excerpt: A small bronze plaque marks the spot.

facts.text: The hotel uses GeniLac, a network that uses Lake Geneva water to cool and heat buildings.
facts.excerpt: It has adopted the so-called GeniLac programme, a thermal-exchange network that uses water from Lake Geneva to cool and heat local buildings.

facts.text: Honey at breakfast comes from beehives the hotel sponsors in nearby Satigny.
facts.excerpt: The hotel also sponsors three Les Miels de Stéphanie beehives in nearby Satigny, which provide the honey served at breakfast.

facts.text: The entire hotel is wheelchair-accessible, and lifts serve all floors.
facts.excerpt: The entire hotel is wheelchair-accessible, with special entrances off the Quai du Mont-Blanc to the lobby and the key public areas

facts.text: The hotel holds more than 150 angels in various forms, painted, sculpted and carved.
facts.excerpt: The Beau-Rivage has a permanent population of more than 150 angels in various forms—painted, sculpted, carved.

facts.text: The concierge desk has long trained future holders of the Clefs d'Or.
facts.excerpt: The concierge desk at the Beau-Rivage has long served as a sort of finishing school for future holders of the coveted Clefs d'Or.
